intro: Week 10 opens with an NFL game in Munich at 9:30 a.m. ET, and the Chiefs say Patrick Mahomes is on track after an elbow scare. Denver rests at 7-2 with a record streak of one-score wins, while Indianapolis tore down its receiver room. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Colts ship Keenan Allen and Josh Downs to contenders
top.dek: Indianapolis sent Allen to San Francisco and Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday and took back picks in the fourth, fifth and sixth rounds of the 2027 draft. With Alec Pierce on injured reserve, the Colts are thin at receiver heading into Sunday's game against Miami.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Mahomes practices fully after elbow scare
top.dek: An MRI showed no major damage to the throwing elbow Mahomes hurt against the Jets. He was a full participant Friday with no game status. Running back Kenneth Walker is questionable with a groin injury and tackle Jaylon Moore is out.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: CeeDee Lamb catches 10 for 195 and a record
top.dek: Lamb scored once against Indianapolis. His 10 catches lifted his career total to 641, the most by any player before turning 28. He also lost a late fumble, so Dallas wants the yards without the mistakes against San Francisco.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 16: straight one-score wins for the Broncos, an NFL record
top.dek: Denver has won 16 consecutive regular-season games decided by one score, the longest such streak in league history. The latest came against Carolina, when the Broncos took the lead in the fourth quarter. They are 7-2 and on their bye.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Patriots and Lions kick off in Munich at 9:30 a.m. ET
top.dek: New England plays the 6-2 Lions on FOX at FC Bayern Munich Stadium. Detroit's offense averages 27.8 points, fifth in the league, against a Patriots pass defense ranked 25th. Watch Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills 7-1 after beating Vikings, now visit Jets

stories.text: Bills improve to 7-1 with a 23-6 win at Minnesota
stories.summary: Buffalo controlled the ball for more than 42 minutes on Monday night and held Minnesota to 178 yards. It is the Bills' best eight-game start since 1993. The defense forced three turnovers, and Josh Allen threw a 25-yard touchdown to Keleki Latu just before halftime.

stories.text: Spencer Brown doubtful for Jets, Dawkins and Anderson back
stories.summary: Right tackle Spencer Brown (ankle) did not practice Thursday or Friday and is doubtful, so Tylan Grable would likely start. Cornerback Christian Benford (wrist), Sam Franklin Jr. (shoulder) and Jordan Hancock (hamstring) are questionable. Left tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs) and left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) practiced Friday and look on track to play.

stories.text: James Cook grinds out 107 yards on 31 carries
stories.summary: Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards and a late touchdown in Minnesota. He now ranks fifth in the NFL with 814 rushing yards. Buffalo leans on him again Sunday against the Jets.

stories.text: 24: Tyler Bass has made 24 straight field goals
stories.summary: Bass hit three more field goals in Minnesota and stretched his franchise-record streak to 24 in a row. Allen also reached 322 regular-season touchdowns, tying Peyton Manning for the most by a player in his first 10 seasons.

stories.text: Bills visit the 2-7 Jets Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo has won five straight against New York and 10 of the last 12. The Bills added safety Amani Hooker in a trade with Tennessee on Tuesday, and he shares the NFL lead with five interceptions. Watch how the Bills handle rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who has 7.5 sacks.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: McCord makes first start as Willis hits IR

stories.text: Kyle McCord gets first NFL start with Willis on IR
stories.summary: Miami placed Malik Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury, and he will miss at least Weeks 10 through 13. McCord, 24, arrived in an offseason trade with Green Bay and takes over a 1-7 team at Indianapolis. Backup Brady Cook will likely be elevated from the practice squad.

stories.text: Aaron Brewer out with concussion, Jared Wayne out
stories.summary: Center Aaron Brewer (concussion) and receiver Jared Wayne (quad) are out for Sunday. Receiver Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful and cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. (knee) is questionable. Andrew Meyer will likely make his first start of the season at center.

stories.text: Rookie Caleb Douglas becomes McCord's top target
stories.summary: Douglas caught six of eight targets for 70 yards in the loss to Detroit. He told reporters he and McCord have built strong chemistry on the scout team, and both say they are ready to compete Sunday.

stories.text: 11: penalties for 87 yards cost Miami against Detroit
stories.summary: The Dolphins held the Lions to 270 yards and a 25 percent third-down rate in the 19-9 loss. They also took 11 penalties for 87 yards, which erased much of that defensive work.

stories.text: Dolphins visit the 2-7 Colts Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Miami (1-7) plays at Lucas Oil Stadium against an Indianapolis team that has lost five straight. Watch McCord's first start, a patched offensive line and whether the Dolphins clean up the penalties.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots chase a fast start in Munich

stories.text: Patriots head to Munich needing a fast start vs. Lions
stories.summary: New England (5-4) faces Detroit in Germany after a 45-27 home loss to Green Bay in which it trailed 17-0 early in the second quarter. The Patriots have fallen behind early against the Bears, Dolphins and Packers. Mike Vrabel's team has played 10 straight weeks without a bye.

stories.text: Brown and Stevenson questionable, Henderson out
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle, knee) and running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) are questionable, and Mike Vrabel said both looked pretty good in practice. Guard Ben Brown, cornerback Carlton Davis III and running back TreVeyon Henderson are out. Henderson spent several days in the hospital for tests on neurological symptoms, and Vrabel gave no return timetable.

stories.text: Drake Maye has three touchdowns in six straight games
stories.summary: Maye has thrown 18 touchdown passes and produced at least three total touchdowns in six straight games. He also threw three interceptions against Green Bay, so Detroit's defense will test how he protects the ball.

stories.text: -11: Patriots turnover differential ranks 31st
stories.summary: New England is minus-11 in turnover margin, tied for 31st in the league. Detroit sits at plus-3. Vrabel said it is tough to play defense in this league without creating turnovers.

stories.text: Patriots face the 6-2 Lions in Munich at 9:30 a.m. on FOX
stories.summary: The game kicks off Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET at FC Bayern Munich Stadium. New England ranks 25th against the pass and Detroit's offense averages 27.8 points, fifth in the league. Watch Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs against a defense that has struggled to take the ball away.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets 2-7, Glenn under fire before Bills

stories.text: Aaron Glenn feels the heat as Jets slide to 2-7
stories.summary: The Jets have lost four straight after a 35-12 defeat to Kansas City, and Glenn is 5-21 in his season and a half as head coach. Speculation about his job is growing. Glenn said the team feels it is on the cusp of breaking through.

stories.text: Garrett Wilson questionable, Trevin Wallace out
stories.summary: Linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) is out. Eight Jets are questionable, including receivers Garrett Wilson (concussion), Adonai Mitchell (knee) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), plus edge Joseph Ossai (ankle) and lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle). Wilson, Cooper and Ossai were full participants Friday.

stories.text: Rookie David Bailey sets the pace with 7.5 sacks
stories.summary: The No. 2 overall pick had two sacks and two forced fumbles on Patrick Mahomes in the loss to Kansas City. Bailey shares the NFL lead with five forced fumbles. Bills coach Joe Brady called him already a star.

stories.text: 13: Jets lead the NFL in forced fumbles
stories.summary: The Jets defense has forced 13 fumbles, the most in the league. The offense has scored on its opening possession in five straight games, but five of seven losses came by a combined 25 points.

stories.text: Jets host the 7-1 Bills Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at MetLife Stadium. Geno Smith needs a rebound after throwing for 165 yards and no touchdowns and taking five sacks against Kansas City. New York also has to slow Buffalo's run game and stop settling for red zone field goals.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Brissett gets the Ravens' fourth QB start in four weeks

stories.text: Ravens turn to Jacoby Brissett as fourth starting QB in four weeks
stories.summary: Baltimore acquired Brissett from Arizona on Nov. 6, and he first practiced with the team Wednesday. He will start Monday night against the winless Chargers. The Ravens have lost four straight and need a spark to keep their season alive.

stories.text: Jackson and Huntley stay out as Bateman, Hawkins, Ioane work limited
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first offensive play against the Bills on Nov. 1 and is out long term. Tyler Huntley is also out after toe surgery. Rashod Bateman (calf), Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) and Olaivavega Ioane (knee/shoulder) were limited Thursday.

stories.text: Jacoby Brissett arrives in Baltimore with a 3-5 mark this season
stories.summary: The 33-year-old has 73 career starts over 11 seasons. He is 3-5 as a starter this season, and Zay Flowers praised his communication with receivers. Flowers has just three catches for 6 yards over the past two games, so Brissett has work to do.

stories.text: 117-43: the margin the Ravens have been outscored during a four-game skid
stories.summary: Baltimore lost 36-10 to the Bills and 33-10 to the Jaguars in the last two games of the slide. The Ravens sit at 4-5. Their offense has to find points with a new quarterback.

stories.text: Ravens host winless Chargers on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Baltimore hosts Los Angeles (0-8) Monday, Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. First-year coach Jesse Minter faces his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time. Watch whether Brissett and Flowers connect early.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals chase AFC North lead on Sunday night

stories.text: Bengals and Steelers meet at 6-2 with the AFC North lead on the line
stories.summary: Cincinnati rides a four-game winning streak and its best start since 2015 into Sunday night. The Bengals beat Atlanta 31-17 in Madrid last week. A win would put them alone atop the division.

stories.text: Dugger ruled out as three Bengals return from injured reserve
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) is out. Jalen Davis, Andrei Iosivas and Brian Parker II were cleared to practice and are listed doubtful, with roster activation decisions due Saturday. Guard Dylan Fairchild (pectoral) was a full participant Friday.

stories.text: Joe Burrow leads the NFL in three passing categories
stories.summary: Burrow tops the league in completion rate, passing yards per game and touchdown passes. He has thrown at least three touchdowns in each of the last four games. He threw for 282 yards and three scores in the Week 3 loss at Pittsburgh.

stories.text: 4: straight games of 30 or more points for Cincinnati
stories.summary: The Bengals have scored at least 30 in each of their four wins, the first time they have done that in a four-game winning streak. Chase, Higgins and Mike Gesicki each have at least six receiving touchdowns through eight games. Only the 2013 Broncos had another trio like it.

stories.text: Bengals host Steelers on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Cincinnati hosts Pittsburgh Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Bengals rank 25th against the run and allow 5.04 yards per carry, the most in the NFL. Watch how they handle Jaylen Warren.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Monken sticks with Watson over Sanders vs. Texans

stories.text: Browns keep Deshaun Watson as the starter over Shedeur Sanders
stories.summary: Coach Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Sunday after Sanders led a comeback in a 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. Monken said he planned all along to go back to Watson, who is 5-3 in eight starts. Sanders had not taken first-team reps in about 10 weeks.

stories.text: Denzel Boston questionable with toe injury, Hickman out
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Denzel Boston is questionable with a toe injury, though Monken said he looked good in Friday's practice. Safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Michael Burton are out. Rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren will start next to Grant Delpit.

stories.text: Denzel Boston leads Browns with 507 receiving yards
stories.summary: Boston has 32 catches for 507 yards and is second on the team with three touchdown catches. He caught a 60-yard pass from Sanders against the Saints. His toe will decide whether he plays Sunday.

stories.text: 33: sacks taken by Watson, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, 7 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. His sack total leads the league. Houston ties Minnesota for the NFL lead with 29.0 sacks, so pressure is the matchup to watch.

stories.text: Browns host Texans on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Cleveland hosts Houston Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Texans have won three of four after an 0-4 start. It is Watson's second start against his former team.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers face Bengals for the AFC North lead

stories.text: Steelers come off the bye with first place in the AFC North at stake
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-2, has won four straight and takes the field Sunday night at Cincinnati, also 6-2. The Steelers won the first meeting 30-27 on Sept. 27. Mike Tomlin, who resigned after last season, will be there as an NBC analyst.

stories.text: Derrick Harmon questionable with foot injury but practiced fully
stories.summary: Harmon is the only Steelers player with a game status. He took part fully on Friday. T.J. Watt, Cameron Heyward and Darnell Washington were full participants with rest designations.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren leads the NFL at 5.92 yards per carry
stories.summary: Warren is having a career year. He piled up 176 scrimmage yards in the first meeting with Cincinnati, including 49 receiving. He has two 100-yard games against the Bengals in the last three meetings.

stories.text: 85: Aaron Rodgers' touchdown passes on Sunday nights, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Rodgers owns the league high for Sunday night touchdown passes. Pittsburgh also has 18 road wins on Sunday nights, tied for second most. The Steelers pass offense has struggled to produce downfield this season.

stories.text: Steelers visit Bengals on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays at Cincinnati Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch how the Steelers pass rush handles Joe Burrow. Pittsburgh has sacked him 24 times in eight meetings.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Stroud's five TDs lift Texans to 3-1 run

stories.text: Stroud throws five touchdowns as Texans rout winless Chargers
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud went 21 of 35 for 384 yards and five touchdown passes in a 44-22 win at the Chargers on Nov. 8. Houston has won three of its last four after an 0-4 start. The Texans now sit 3-5 and head to Cleveland.

stories.text: Hunter and Harrison Jr. out at Cleveland, Anderson questionable
stories.summary: The Texans ruled out DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring), WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), LB Azeez Al-Shaair, TE Brevin Jordan and interior lineman Keylan Rutledge. DE Will Anderson Jr. (ankle), T Trent Brown, G Wyatt Teller, RB David Montgomery, LB Jake Hummel and CB Jaylin Smith are questionable.

stories.text: Tre' Boutte scores twice, including a 63-yard strike
stories.summary: Receiver Tre' Boutte caught two of Stroud's five touchdowns against the Chargers, a 12-yarder before halftime and a 63-yarder early in the fourth quarter. Tank Dell and Nico Collins also scored through the air. Boutte's role grows with Harrison out Sunday.

stories.text: 8: sacks the Texans piled up on the Chargers
stories.summary: Houston sacked the Chargers eight times in the Week 9 rout. Sheldon Rankins, Jadeveon Clowney and Will Anderson Jr. each took down the quarterback twice. The defense also forced two turnovers, including a Derek Stingley Jr. interception.

stories.text: Texans visit Browns Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Houston plays at Cleveland on Nov. 15 at Huntington Bank Field. The Browns are 5-4 and 3-0 at home, while the Texans are 3-1 on the road. Watch the Houston pass rush if Hunter is out and Anderson is limited.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts deal Allen and Downs, thin at receiver

stories.text: Colts trade Keenan Allen and Josh Downs after the deadline
stories.summary: Indianapolis sent Allen to San Francisco and Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday. The Colts got picks in the fourth, fifth and sixth rounds of the 2027 draft. Alec Pierce is on injured reserve, so the receiver room is stripped down.

stories.text: Taylor clear for Dolphins; five Colts out Wednesday and Thursday
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor came off the injury report and is set to play. Mo Alie-Cox, Jaylon Carlies, Akeem Davis-Gaither, long snapper Luke Rhodes and tackle Jalen Travis did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Jerry Tillery (calf) did not practice Thursday.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor has 656 yards but only 8 carries at Jacksonville
stories.summary: Taylor has 161 carries for 656 yards and 8 touchdowns, plus 26 catches for 220 yards. He got just eight carries in the 42-7 loss at Jacksonville. He has 69 rushing yards over the last two games.

stories.text: 215: yards for Laquon Treadwell, the top remaining Colts receiver
stories.summary: Treadwell has 16 catches for 215 yards on 29 targets, the most among the receivers left after the trades. Allen and Downs combined for 73 catches and 705 yards. Deion Burks has 60 yards and Alec Pierce has 72 on injured reserve.

stories.text: Colts host Dolphins Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Indianapolis (2-7) hosts Miami (1-7) at Lucas Oil Stadium on Nov. 15. The Dolphins start Kyle McCord, who has not thrown a regular-season pass, after Malik Willis went to injured reserve. Watch how Daniel Jones moves the ball with Tyler Warren and a thin receiver group.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars bench Bates and Davis at Tennessee

stories.text: Jaguars rest new defenders Bates and Davis against Titans
stories.summary: Coach Liam Coen said safety Jessie Bates and tackle Jordan Davis, both deadline acquisitions, will not play at Tennessee. Neither has had a bye yet this season. Jacksonville is a double-digit favorite and leads the AFC South by three games.

stories.text: Tuten sat Thursday with ankle and foot issue; Green nears return
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten did not practice Thursday with an ankle and foot injury. Guard Ezra Cleveland, safety Antonio Johnson, running back Chris Rodriguez Jr., center Robert Hainsey and linebacker Branson Combs were limited. Defensive end BJ Green practiced fully again and is set to return from injured reserve.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence owns the NFL's second-best passer rating
stories.summary: Lawrence has 18 touchdown passes, four interceptions and a 111.7 passer rating through eight games. That rating ranks second in the league. He threw no interceptions in the last two games.

stories.text: +7: Jaguars lead the NFL in turnover differential
stories.summary: Jacksonville has 15 takeaways this season after three against Baltimore in the 33-10 win. Under defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, the Jaguars have 46 takeaways in 25 games, up from nine in all of 2024. They did it without nose tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray.

stories.text: Jaguars visit Titans Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Jacksonville (6-2) plays at Tennessee (1-7) at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15. The teams meet again Nov. 29 in Jacksonville. Lawrence threw for 484 yards and five touchdowns in two games against the Titans last season.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans off bye, thin at guard vs Jaguars

stories.text: Cam Ward posts first 300-yard game in overtime loss to Cincinnati
stories.summary: Ward went 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns in the 43-36 overtime loss on Nov. 1. He also ran for 41 yards and threw a two-point conversion. The Titans, coming off a Week 9 bye, are 1-7 and host Jacksonville.

stories.text: Skoronski, Tate and two linebackers out against Jacksonville
stories.summary: Tennessee ruled out guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), linebackers Cody Barton and Anthony Hill Jr., and punter Tommy Townsend. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable after a full Friday practice.

stories.text: Tony Pollard runs for 117 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Pollard carried 21 times for 117 yards and two touchdowns against the Bengals, his second straight 100-yard game. He added 20 receiving yards. He also scored on a 40-yard run in the first quarter.

stories.text: 36: points scored at Cincinnati, a Titans high since 2021
stories.summary: Tennessee scored 36 points against the Bengals, its most since October 2021. Safety Amani Hooker intercepted Joe Burrow three times, and Jacob Martin had three sacks. The Titans still lost after Burrow tied it with 1:17 left and won in overtime.

stories.text: Titans host Jaguars Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee hosts Jacksonville at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15 in Music City uniforms. The Jaguars are 6-2 and double-digit favorites. The rematch comes Nov. 29 at EverBank Stadium.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos take a five-game streak into the bye

stories.text: Broncos beat Panthers 26-21 for a fifth straight win
stories.summary: Denver went to Charlotte and won 26-21 to reach 7-2, with three straight road wins. A Sean Payton challenge turned a Carolina catch at the goal line into a Devon Key interception, and the Broncos drove 80 yards for a touchdown after it. Nik Bonitto's late strip-sack closed the game before Denver heads into its bye.

stories.text: Waddle and Moss leave Carolina game with concussions
stories.summary: Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle took a hit from safety Zakee Wheatley on a downfield pass and left in the first half with a concussion. Cornerback Riley Moss also suffered a concussion and did not return. Pat Bryant, back from injured reserve, led the Denver receivers with 56 yards. The bye gives both concussed players extra time before the Nov. 22 game.

stories.text: Bonitto's strip-sack seals Denver's win in Charlotte
stories.summary: Nik Bonitto stripped Bryce Young with under 90 seconds left and Denver recovered at its own 44. It was Bonitto's first strip-sack of the season. Bo Nix then scored on a one-yard sneak three plays later to put the game away.

stories.text: 16: straight one-score wins, an NFL record
stories.summary: Denver has won 16 consecutive regular-season games decided by one score, the longest such streak in NFL history. The Panthers game fit the pattern, with the Broncos taking the lead in the fourth quarter. They also converted 6 of 10 third downs, their best mark of the year.

stories.text: Broncos rest in Week 10, then host the Raiders Nov. 22
stories.summary: Denver is on its bye this weekend. The Broncos return home on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS against the Las Vegas Raiders. Kansas City sits half a game back in the AFC West, so the division race stays tight through the break.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs snap skid; Mahomes elbow improving

stories.text: Chiefs snap two-game skid with 35-12 win over Jets
stories.summary: Kansas City ended a two-game losing streak by beating the Jets 35-12 at Arrowhead. Patrick Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns after a late first-half scare, and the defense piled up a season-high five sacks. The win moved the Chiefs to 6-2, half a game behind Denver.

stories.text: Mahomes practices fully after elbow scare
stories.summary: Mahomes hurt his throwing elbow against the Jets, and an MRI showed no major damage. Friday's report lists him as a full participant with a knee and right elbow designation and no game status. Offensive tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) is out, and running back Kenneth Walker (groin) is questionable. Wide receiver Xavier Worthy, who left the Jets game with a hamstring injury, practiced fully.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker scores three times against the Jets
stories.summary: Walker ran 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown, then caught four passes for 41 yards and two more scores. He finished with 143 scrimmage yards and 1,044 for the season, the first Chief over 1,000 since Isiah Pacheco in 2023. It was his fifth multi-touchdown game of the year, the most in the NFL.

stories.text: 9,360: Mahomes and Kelce set the QB-to-TE yards record
stories.summary: Mahomes and Travis Kelce now hold the NFL record for passing yards from a quarterback to a tight end, at 9,360. Kelce led the Chiefs with 72 receiving yards against the Jets and added a one-yard rushing touchdown. Fifty-six of those yards came after the catch.

stories.text: Chiefs visit the 3-6 Falcons on Sunday
stories.summary: Kansas City plays at Atlanta on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Mahomes said after practice this week that he has no doubts about playing. Watch the pass rush, which hit Geno Smith on half his dropbacks last week, against a Falcons team that is 3-6.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza gets the keys after Cousins trade

stories.text: Raiders trade Cousins, hand rookie Mendoza the starting job
stories.summary: Las Vegas sent quarterback Kirk Cousins to Minnesota for a 2027 third-round pick before Tuesday's deadline. That puts No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza in the huddle for his first career start against Seattle. The Raiders are 4-5 after opening 3-0 and losing five of their last six.

stories.text: Booker and Thornton questionable for Seattle
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Thomas Booker practiced fully Friday after two limited days and is questionable. Dont'e Thornton joined the report Friday after missing practice and is also questionable. Guard Trey Zuhn, who carried a concussion-related listing earlier in the week, practiced fully Friday.

stories.text: Brock Bowers eyes another 100-yard game
stories.summary: The Raiders' tight end needs one more 100-yard receiving game to reach eight, which would pass Rob Gronkowski and tie Kellen Winslow for the second most by a tight end through 37 career games. Bowers fumbled in last week's loss to San Francisco, so he also has a ball-security issue to fix. A rookie quarterback will lean on him Sunday.

stories.text: 31st: Raiders rank near the bottom in rushing, 5th in passing
stories.summary: Las Vegas averages 259.7 passing yards a game, fifth in the NFL, but only 71.3 rushing yards, 31st. The offense still scores 26.4 points a game, eighth in the league. Mendoza's first start will test whether that balance holds without Cousins.

stories.text: Raiders host Seahawks Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Mendoza makes his first NFL start at Allegiant Stadium against 5-4 Seattle. He has one NFL appearance, 6 of 8 for 48 yards in mop-up time at New England. Seattle plans to start Drew Lock again while Sam Darnold recovers from quad and rib injuries.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers visit Baltimore on Monday night

stories.text: Herbert sacked eight times as Chargers fall to 0-8
stories.summary: Houston beat Los Angeles 44-22 as Justin Herbert took a career-high eight sacks. C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. The Chargers have lost 11 straight games dating to last season, and Jim Harbaugh called the result a bitter pill to swallow.

stories.text: X-rays on Herbert's hand clear; McConkey day-to-day
stories.summary: Harbaugh said X-rays on Herbert's non-throwing hand came back negative and the quarterback should be fine. Ladd McConkey was active against Houston but did not play because of back spasms, and Harbaugh called him day-to-day. Isas Waxter, Cam Hart and Justin Eboigbe left the game with ankle injuries.

stories.text: Quentin Johnston ends the touchdown drought
stories.summary: Johnston turned a Herbert pass into a 58-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, the Chargers' first touchdown since Week 5. By then Houston led 38-9. Herbert finished 13 of 23 for 193 yards and has thrown 11 interceptions, the most in the NFL.

stories.text: 37: drives without a touchdown before Johnston's catch
stories.summary: The Chargers went 12 straight quarters and 37 offensive drives without a touchdown, from Oct. 11 until the fourth quarter Sunday. That is the second-longest such streak in NFL history, behind the 2000 Baltimore Ravens at 61 drives. Los Angeles also went 5 of 17 on third down.

stories.text: Chargers visit the Ravens on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Baltimore (4-5) on Monday, Nov. 16, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Herbert is expected to play. The Chargers then return home to face the Jets on Nov. 22.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys host 49ers off a win over Indy

stories.text: Cowboys escape Indianapolis and now face the 7-1 49ers
stories.summary: Dallas beat the Colts 27-23 when Javonte Williams punched in a one-yard touchdown with just over a minute left, then Caleb Downs picked off Daniel Jones to end it. The Cowboys sit at 4-5 and want back-to-back wins for the first time in a while. San Francisco comes to AT&T Stadium at 7-1 and has beaten Dallas four straight times.

stories.text: Pickens clears the report, but the secondary is thin
stories.summary: George Pickens came off the injury report Friday and is expected to play after missing last week's game. Tight end Jake Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson are out. Cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. and DaRon Bland are both questionable, and safety Juanyeh Thomas is doubtful.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb piles up 195 yards and a record
stories.summary: Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown against Indianapolis. The 10 catches pushed his career total to 641, the most by any player before turning 28. He also lost a late fumble, so the Cowboys want the yards without the mistakes this week.

stories.text: 14: Penalties the Cowboys took in Indianapolis
stories.summary: Dallas drew 14 flags for 153 yards in the win over the Colts. Dak Prescott said the team must clean that up against a San Francisco defense that ranks sixth in points allowed at 19.5 per game. The Cowboys also have not yet beaten a team with a winning record this season.

stories.text: 49ers visit AT&T Stadium Sunday at 4:25 ET
stories.summary: Dallas hosts San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch whether the Cowboys protect Prescott against Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner, and whether they stop Christian McCaffrey in the passing game. Quinnen Williams has 4 sacks over his last four games.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lose a Thursday night lead late

stories.text: Giants blow a late lead to Washington on Thursday night
stories.summary: New York led 21-17 midway through the fourth quarter before Jayden Daniels drove Washington 71 yards in three plays and hit Stefon Diggs for the winning touchdown with 57 seconds left. J.J. McCarthy threw for a career-high 293 yards, but Rasul Douglas intercepted his last pass. The Giants still lead the NFC East at 5-3-1.

stories.text: Safety Jason Pinnock leaves with a back injury
stories.summary: Pinnock left early in the third quarter Thursday with a back injury, and the game coverage gave no update on his status. Linebacker Malik Harrison carried a questionable tag for the game with a groin issue. The Giants have 10 days before they host Jacksonville.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely turns in nine catches for 127 yards
stories.summary: Likely caught nine passes for 127 yards and the 66-yard touchdown that put New York ahead in the fourth quarter. Cam Skattebo added 78 yards and two touchdowns on 18 carries. Neither could keep the Giants from losing in the closing minute.

stories.text: 399: Giants yards in a loss they outgained
stories.summary: New York outgained Washington 399 to 340 on Thursday but lost the turnover battle with two giveaways. A 33-yard pass interference call on Deonte Banks set up the winning drive. A delay of game on fourth-and-1 and a missed field goal also hurt.

stories.text: Jaguars visit MetLife Nov. 22 at 4:25 ET
stories.summary: The Giants host Jacksonville on Sunday, Nov. 22. The NFL moved the game from 1 p.m. to 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. New York needs to tighten its late-game clock management before the Jaguars arrive.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles use the bye to regroup at 2-7

stories.text: Eagles enter the bye 2-7 with Hurts done for the year
stories.summary: Philadelphia has lost seven straight and has less than a 1 percent chance at the playoffs, according to NBC Sports Philadelphia. Jalen Hurts went on injured reserve with blood clots that the outlet says will end his season. Tanner McKee and then Joe Milton have taken his snaps.

stories.text: Eagles down to one healthy running back
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley is the only running back on the active roster after the Eagles waived Jaydon Blue this week. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are on injured reserve. Linebacker Zack Baun also left Sunday's loss to the Giants early with a back injury.

stories.text: Jalen Carter leads a defense that keeps improving
stories.summary: Carter has 5 sacks, 4 forced fumbles and 7 tackles for loss this season. The defensive line produced six sacks of Giants quarterbacks last Sunday. The group has played well enough to win while the offense has not.

stories.text: 7: Sacks Joe Milton took in the loss to New York
stories.summary: Milton went 18 of 34 for 169 yards and led the Eagles with 64 rushing yards on nine carries. Philadelphia gained zero yards in the third quarter of the 19-11 loss. Nick Sirianni said the team has to figure out its offense.

stories.text: Eagles host Steelers Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Philadelphia is on its bye this week. The Eagles return to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Nov. 22 against Pittsburgh. The NFL moved kickoff to 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Diggs and Daniels steal one at MetLife

stories.text: Daniels and Diggs rally Washington past the Giants
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions, then led a three-play, 71-yard drive that ended with a 32-yard touchdown to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left. Rasul Douglas then intercepted J.J. McCarthy to seal the 24-21 win. Washington is 3-5-1 and two games behind the Giants.

stories.text: Patrick and Yankoff out, Okonkwo returns
stories.summary: Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and tight end Colson Yankoff (knee) were ruled out Thursday, and Nick Allegretti started at center. Tight end Chig Okonkwo left with a back injury in the second quarter and came back after halftime.

stories.text: Sonny Styles piles up 13 tackles in the win
stories.summary: The rookie linebacker made 13 tackles Thursday, including a third-down tackle for loss on McCarthy in the fourth quarter. He leads Washington with 80 tackles this season. His 19 percent pressure rate is the best among rookie defenders.

stories.text: 4 for 4: Ben Sinnott's night after one catch all year
stories.summary: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown that gave Washington a 10-7 lead late in the first half. He had only one catch before Thursday. The defense has also held its last four opponents to 23 points or fewer.

stories.text: Bengals visit Monday, Nov. 23 at 8:15 ET
stories.summary: Washington hosts Cincinnati on Monday night, Nov. 23, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Commanders get extra rest after Thursday's game. Watch whether the line holds up with Patrick's concussion status unsettled.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears hit the bye 7-2 and atop the North

stories.text: Bears reach the bye at 7-2 and in first place
stories.summary: Chicago has won four straight and leads the NFC North, but it is 0-2 against division teams so far. Four of its final eight games are against the North, so the standings will get settled in those matchups.

stories.text: Bears use the bye to heal Monangai, Burden and Williams
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai has missed time with a toe injury and is expected back for New Orleans. Receiver Luther Burden III left the Tampa Bay game with a concussion, and quarterback Caleb Williams gets a week to rest his hamstring.

stories.text: Williams survives four picks and drives Chicago to a win
stories.summary: Williams went 22 of 37 for 279 yards and two touchdowns against Tampa Bay despite four interceptions. He then led an eight-play, 49-yard drive that set up Cairo Santos for a 38-yard field goal as time expired.

stories.text: 22.8%: Bears hold the league's lowest third-down rate
stories.summary: Opponents convert only 22.8 percent of their third downs against Chicago, the lowest rate in the NFL by a wide margin. Tampa Bay went 2 for 12 on third down in the last game.

stories.text: Bears are on bye, then host the Saints on Nov. 22
stories.summary: Chicago does not play this week. The Bears return Sunday, Nov. 22 at Soldier Field against New Orleans, with Monangai expected back in the backfield.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions fly to Munich with Goff and Branch cleared

stories.text: Lions play the Patriots in Munich on Sunday
stories.summary: Detroit is 6-2 and takes on New England at Allianz Arena in Germany. Quarterback Jared Goff has no injury designation for the game, which Fox will carry.

stories.text: Lions list St. Brown questionable, rule out three
stories.summary: Receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) are questionable. Safety Kerby Joseph, center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed are out, while Goff (chest) and safety Brian Branch (hip) practiced fully.

stories.text: Gibbs leads the Lions with 1,132 scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Running back Jahmyr Gibbs has 1,132 yards from scrimmage and 11 touchdowns through eight games. He is Goff's main backfield option against a Patriots team that just allowed 45 points to Green Bay.

stories.text: 15 to 2: Goff's touchdown-to-interception ratio
stories.summary: Goff has thrown 15 touchdown passes against two interceptions this season. St. Brown has 61 catches for 657 yards and five touchdowns alongside him.

stories.text: Lions face the Patriots at 9:30 a.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Detroit kicks off Sunday morning in Munich. New England arrives after a 45-27 loss to Green Bay, and Detroit's offense will test a Patriots defense that struggles against play-action.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers host Vikings without Jacobs and Parsons

stories.text: Packers host Minnesota with five wins in six games
stories.summary: Green Bay is 6-3 after a 45-27 win at New England and welcomes the Vikings to Lambeau Field on Sunday. Minnesota has blitzed Jordan Love more than any team has blitzed a quarterback this year.

stories.text: Packers rule out Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Whyle
stories.summary: Running back Josh Jacobs (finger), edge Micah Parsons, center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) are out. Linebacker Zaire Franklin is doubtful, and seven players are questionable, including safety Xavier McKinney.

stories.text: Love throws for 372 yards and four total touchdowns
stories.summary: Jordan Love went 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the win at New England, and he added a rushing score. Christian Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards and Matthew Golden had 10 for 164, both career highs.

stories.text: 129: Packers finally top 100 rushing yards
stories.summary: Green Bay ran for 129 yards on 32 carries at New England, its first 100-yard rushing game of the season. The Packers entered the day last in the NFL in rushing.

stories.text: Packers host the Vikings at Lambeau on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Green Bay meets Minnesota in a Fox game at noon Central. Watch how the Packers cover for Jacobs and Parsons against a Vikings team with a new quarterback.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Cousins gets the call at Lambeau

stories.text: Cousins will start for Minnesota at Green Bay
stories.summary: The Vikings got Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas for a 2027 third-round pick before the deadline. Head coach Kevin O'Connell named him the starter for Sunday's game at Lambeau Field.

stories.text: Vikings list Murray, Hockenson and Jennings among five out
stories.summary: Quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), tight end T.J. Hockenson, receiver Jauan Jennings, linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) and lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins are out. Receiver Jordan Addison, safety Josh Metellus and Kyle Van Noy are questionable.

stories.text: Cousins brings 20 touchdowns from Las Vegas
stories.summary: In nine starts for the Raiders this season, Cousins averaged 260 passing yards per game and threw 20 touchdowns. He played in Minnesota from 2018 to 2023 and now steps in for an injured Murray.

stories.text: 8.9: Wentz's passer rating in the loss to Buffalo
stories.summary: Carson Wentz went 8 of 25 for 81 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble in the 23-6 loss to the Bills. Minnesota then reacquired Cousins before the trade deadline.

stories.text: Vikings visit the Packers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Minnesota plays at Lambeau Field after two straight losses. The Vikings start a new quarterback and work around a thin list of healthy skill players.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons seek a spark against Chiefs

stories.text: Falcons limp into Chiefs game at 3-6 after Madrid loss
stories.summary: Atlanta dropped its fourth game in five tries, 34-17 to Cincinnati at the Bernabeu. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 162 yards with one touchdown and one interception, a week after four picks against Tampa Bay. Kicker Nick Folk also missed a 38-yarder, his fifth miss in nine games.

stories.text: Branch out, Deablo doubtful for Falcons against Chiefs
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Zachariah Branch will miss Sunday with a hamstring injury, and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) is doubtful. Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter (illness), edge rusher James Pearce Jr. (back) and linebacker Josh Woods (ankle) are all questionable.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson hits 100 rushing yards again in Madrid
stories.summary: Robinson ran 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and added six catches for 47 more. The Falcons piled up 157 rushing yards as a team, their first 100-yard rushing day since Week 4. Penix also scrambled for a career-high 50 yards.

stories.text: 5: Nick Folk misses in nine games for Atlanta
stories.summary: Folk pushed a 38-yard field goal in Madrid, his fifth miss of the season through nine games. In a game decided by 17 points the miss cost little, but it adds to a special teams unit under scrutiny. Atlanta also lost Brian Robinson Jr. to injured reserve this week.

stories.text: Falcons host Chiefs Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Atlanta (3-6) hosts Kansas City at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Watch whether the Falcons can protect Penix against a Chiefs pass rush and keep Robinson running, since Patrick Mahomes practiced fully this week after a bruised right elbow.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers chase first place in New Orleans

stories.text: Panthers and Saints play for NFC South lead at 3-5
stories.summary: Carolina and New Orleans are both 3-5, so Sunday's winner takes sole possession of first place in the division. Carolina will try to protect Bryce Young, who has taken 26 sacks. Interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash calls his second game since Ejiro Evero was fired on Oct. 30.

stories.text: Jaelan Phillips questionable as Okereke sits again
stories.summary: Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) is out for a second straight game. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips practiced fully Friday and is questionable after missing three weeks with a hamstring strain. Cornerback Will Lee III is also questionable, while Mike Jackson and Jonathon Brooks are doubtful.

stories.text: Bryce Young faces a pass rush that has sacked 26 times
stories.summary: Young has been sacked 26 times this season, yet Carolina ranks fourth in the NFL in passing offense. He is 1-5 all time against New Orleans and 0-3 at the Superdome. Chase Young (8 sacks) and Carl Granderson (7.5) lead the Saints rush.

stories.text: 13 of 14: Ryan Fitzgerald on field goals this season
stories.summary: Fitzgerald missed against Denver in Week 9 for his first failed field goal of the year. Coach Dave Canales said he trusts the kicker, and special teams coordinator Tracy Smith said the misses look alike, which makes them easier to fix. Fitzgerald has also missed five extra points.

stories.text: Panthers visit Saints Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Carolina (3-5) travels to the Caesars Superdome. New Orleans has won five of the last six meetings, including a 20-17 win last December on a field goal with two seconds left. Watch Young against the Saints pass rush and whether Phillips gets back on the field.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints shuffle the line for Panthers

stories.text: Shough's overtime touchdown pass beats Browns, 23-22
stories.summary: Tyler Shough hit Juwan Johnson from 15 yards in overtime, and New Orleans then stopped Cleveland's two-point try to win its first home game of the year. The Saints improved to 3-5 and now share the NFC South lead with Carolina. A win Sunday would give them it outright.

stories.text: Saints lose Fuaga, McCoy; Etienne questionable
stories.summary: Right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee sprain), center Erik McCoy (biceps), running back CJ Donaldson and tackle Christen Miller are out. Coach Kellen Moore said Fuaga's injury is not long term. Cesar Ruiz moves to center, and Travis Etienne is questionable after a full practice Friday.

stories.text: Chase Young leads Saints pass rush with 8 sacks
stories.summary: Young has 8 sacks, and Carl Granderson has 7.5. Together they give New Orleans a real chance to rattle Bryce Young on Sunday. The Saints rank 28th against the pass, so the rush has to get home.

stories.text: 370.5: yards per game the Saints defense allows
stories.summary: New Orleans ranks 29th in total defense at 370.5 yards per game, while Carolina's defense gives up 344.9. The Saints have a turnover margin of minus 6, compared with minus 1 for the Panthers. The offenses are separated by 36.6 yards a game, with Carolina ahead.

stories.text: Saints host Panthers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 3-5 Saints host the 3-5 Panthers at the Superdome with first place in the NFC South on the line. New Orleans has won five of the last six in the series. Watch the offensive line, which is down two starters, and the kicking game.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs rest up after another close loss

stories.text: Bucs hit bye at 3-6, half a game off the division lead
stories.summary: Tampa Bay lost 27-24 at Chicago on a walk-off field goal after tying the game late. All six of its losses came by seven points or fewer. The offense's inability to turn five takeaways into more than 11 points drew the most criticism.

stories.text: Egbuka back from foot injury; Mayfield past thumb
stories.summary: Receiver Emeka Egbuka returned against Chicago after missing two games with a foot injury and caught three passes for 38 yards. Baker Mayfield played his third game since a dislocated right thumb. The bye gives both extra time to recover.

stories.text: Bucky Irving carries the Bucs offense
stories.summary: Irving ran 20 times for 97 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago. He has 825 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns on 167 carries, an average of 4.9 yards. Tampa Bay out-rushed the Bears 126 yards to 72.

stories.text: 16: interceptions by the Bucs defense, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay picked off Caleb Williams four times, the second straight game with four interceptions. Zyon McCollum had two, and Tykee Smith and Alex Anzalone added one each. The offense still went 2 of 12 on third down and took eight penalties.

stories.text: Bucs on bye, then at Lions Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Tampa Bay has no game in Week 10. It visits Detroit on Fox in Week 11, with eight games left. Watch whether the coaches fix the third-down and penalty problems during the break.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Rookie Beck gets first start against Rams

stories.text: Rookie Carson Beck will make his first NFL start against the Rams
stories.summary: Coach Mike LaFleur confirmed the third-round pick takes over after Gardner Minshew went on injured reserve with a season-ending elbow injury. Beck threw 15 for 19 in the Hall of Fame Game before a rib injury ended his preseason. Arizona already traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.

stories.text: Cardinals list center Hjalte Froholdt out with a concussion
stories.summary: Froholdt, who had not missed a game since 2023, is out Sunday along with guard Jon Gaines II and lineman Zach Carter. Cornerback Max Melton and safety Andrew Wingard are questionable. Receivers Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks are already done for the season.

stories.text: Trey McBride gives Beck a safe target
stories.summary: McBride has 73 catches for 598 yards and five touchdowns this season. He caught seven passes for 54 yards in the loss at Seattle. With the receiver room gutted, he will be the first option for a rookie quarterback.

stories.text: 28.3: Points Arizona allows per game, 31st in the NFL
stories.summary: The Cardinals own the league's second-worst scoring defense at 28.3 points per game. Their offense scores 19.8, which ranks 26th. The Rams enter as 9.5-point favorites.

stories.text: Cardinals host the Rams Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at State Farm Stadium. Watch how Beck handles the Rams' pass defense, which ranks fifth in completion rate allowed. Arizona has lost 11 straight to Seattle and needs a division win.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams hit Arizona without Nacua and Adams

stories.text: Rams face a multi-week hole at receiver
stories.summary: Puka Nacua suffered a significant knee injury in Week 9 and faces a multi-week absence. Davante Adams is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, and Sean McVay called a return after the Week 12 game a realistic timeline. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also out.

stories.text: Avila and Ferguson are out, McDuffie is questionable
stories.summary: Guard Steve Avila (hamstring) and tight end Terrance Ferguson are out. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), who missed Week 9, and safety Kamren Curl are questionable. Edge rusher Myles Garrett (knee) also carries a questionable tag.

stories.text: Matthew Stafford carries the offense
stories.summary: Stafford has thrown for 2,374 yards with 16 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He has averaged 6.4 yards per attempt over his last six games. He threw for 222 yards and two scores against Arizona in Week 6.

stories.text: 20.1: Points the Rams allow per game, eighth in the NFL
stories.summary: The defense gives LA its edge against a Cardinals offense that averages 4.7 yards per play, 28th in the league. The Rams are 9.5-point favorites. Their own offense averages 23.8 points, 13th.

stories.text: Rams visit the Cardinals Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at State Farm Stadium in Glendale. Watch who steps up at receiver and whether McDuffie returns to the secondary. Arizona starts rookie Carson Beck.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers add Keenan Allen and Buckner at deadline

stories.text: 49ers load up at the deadline with Allen and Buckner
stories.summary: San Francisco traded for receiver Keenan Allen and acquired defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from Indianapolis. Allen caught four passes for 26 yards in his first game back against the Colts. The 49ers sit at 7-1, tied for the best record in the league.

stories.text: Mike Evans is out, Trent Williams is questionable
stories.summary: Evans is out with an Achilles injury. Left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (knee) and four cornerbacks, Renardo Green, Nate Hobbs, Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout, are all questionable. Deebo Samuel has no designation and Kyle Shanahan says he is cleared.

stories.text: Christian McCaffrey keeps scoring in bunches
stories.summary: McCaffrey ran 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and caught a touchdown pass in the win over the Raiders. He has scored a rushing touchdown in seven straight games, a 49ers single-season record. He has nine rushing scores this year.

stories.text: 190: Rushing yards the 49ers piled up against Las Vegas
stories.summary: San Francisco ran 43 times, a season high in yards and its most carries since 2022. Shanahan teams are unbeaten when they run 40 or more times. The defense held the Raiders to 24 rushing yards.

stories.text: 49ers visit the Cowboys Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The game is at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. Watch the thin cornerback group against CeeDee Lamb, who has the second-most catches in the league. Dallas is 4-5.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Lock starts for Seattle with Darnold out

stories.text: Drew Lock starts at Las Vegas with Sam Darnold out
stories.summary: Darnold is out with rib and quad injuries, so Lock gets the start despite elbow and oblique issues on the report. Seattle beat Arizona 17-3 last week. The Raiders will start rookie Fernando Mendoza for the first time.

stories.text: Cross, Nelson and Williams join Darnold on the out list
stories.summary: Tackle Charles Cross (ankle), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) are out, as is Darnold. That leaves Seattle thin up front. Jaxon Smith-Njigba sat Wednesday for rest.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba tops 1,000 yards again
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba has 1,036 receiving yards through nine games. He is the third Seahawk with three straight 1,000-yard seasons, after Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent. Zach Charbonnet ran for 77 yards in his second game back from a torn ACL.

stories.text: 11: Straight Seattle wins over Arizona
stories.summary: It is the longest winning streak against one opponent in franchise history. The Cardinals scored 3 points and gained 198 yards on Sunday. Seattle has held three opponents under 200 yards this season.

stories.text: Seahawks visit the Raiders Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Las Vegas allows 234.2 passing yards per game, seventh-worst in the league, so Seattle's receivers should find room. Eight of ten experts in Seattle's preview pick the Seahawks.
